Well, then immediately afterwards, when this wage price was released, where there were strikes for about seven years, there was a strike every year. The flower business, of course, was a luxury business, something you could do without. So it was really kind of rough trying to keep ahead of the, keep the rent paid and what have you in the flower business. And I was offered a job at that time in Spokane where I would have from $20 to $25 a day as a freelance designer. And there were several florists there that assured me they would keep me completely involved. Now, $20 a day was a lot more than I was making in the shop here during that time, my husband and I together. But we owned our own home here. Our son was enrolled in school here. My husband's roots were so deep in this territory that it wouldn't have been sensible or practical, when I thought about it, to remove on the strength of what I alone could do over there. For one thing, he would be extremely unhappy. He could not rate that kind of pay. $20 doesn't sound like much now, but at that time it was big pay. Furthermore, I didn't have to worry about my son here. He showed signs of being an athlete from the time he was eight years old. Here he was involved in baseball all summer long. If he wasn't playing in it, he was watching it. He was thinking it, talking it. During the winter months, he was at the YMCA after school all the time. He was, by the time he was ten years old, he was even permitted to take younger children. Younger children were kept out of the Y as a rule, anyone under ten. But when he was up there, if he would agree to keep charge of them, keep them from really getting wild or mischievous, they would let younger children go in with them. By the time he was 12 years old, he was helping the coaches coach the farm league in baseball. He was always involved in something. He could go to these places without special car transportation. In Spokane, if a boy wants to participate in athletics, somebody is going to have to run a jetty service. This was one of the things I probably considered more than anything else. Prior to that, there had never been any choice. I could not have found anyone to lend me the price of buying myself a little business in a strange town. I was stuck here until I was making money on my own. But I was able to make money on my own because someone had confidence in me. And by the time I had reached the point where I had various offers, it wasn't just that one, that one I gave a lot of consideration to because times were rough right then. But there were various things that made it impossible for me to move, although I could see a lot of advantages from a personal standpoint, but I couldn't see the advantages from a family. And after retirement, I did tentatively try to talk Vance into moving to Coeur d'Alene. I was a little bit selfish in that because I had never ceased pursuing different types of things. I don't have a sense of inferiority any longer because of my lack of education, because I've done many things. I've even had quite a number of articles published, including in the FTD trade journal. And one year they had three of my articles in the course of that year, and they were given the trade journal's top rating for editorial excellence, so I think maybe I wasn't too bad. But I've also had a few other things published, and I hope to do more writing. So I wanted to move to Coeur d'Alene where in the first place I like the town, and I like the air, no smell of smoke. I like gardening. In fact, we've got a backyard garden burned to a crisp out here. But I do quite a little bit of sowing, not because I really like it so well, but because I have to sow my own. I am so out of shape. I mean, there's just not enough up here for down here or the other way around. So the only way I'm comfortable is to do my own sowing. And because of that, my relatives are always bringing in something about the suit, and it's too tight or too loose. And lately I've had some demands from the rest home, and I'm trying to avoid that because the sowing goes back too far into my childhood, in those days when it was an obligatory job always. And there are some instances where I can't discourage it, but I don't mind it for myself. But I find that more and more I get these. I did a couple of shifts for a very dear friend of mine who's just recently in the rest home, and immediately I get requests from several of the others to do something similar, and I'm trying to evade it or avoid it or something.

speaker: Speaker 1
words: Okay, well, I'm going to have to run or we'll get kicked out of our...

speaker: Speaker 2
words: If you...
